title: Harden enterprise access: RBAC schema, SSO/SCIM sync, and review automation
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Deliver a production-grade access controls bundle to meet regulatory evidence needs across data residency boundaries. Scope includes: 1) A clear RBAC role matrix (least privilege) implemented in authz-service and enforced at the model-serving API layer; 2) SSO via SAML (enterprise IdPs) with automated metadata refresh and certificate rotation guidance; 3) SCIM v2.0 provisioning and group sync for user lifecycle (joiners/movers/leavers); 4) Periodic access review automation that emits verifiable evidence artifacts for auditors (signed CSV/ZIP + human-readable report); 5) Tie access events to data residency/retention metadata so audit reports can slice by region/storage class. Exclusions: full UI redesign of Console; federated access across multiple IdPs is out-of-scope for this ticket and will be tracked separately.

acceptance_criteria: SAML SSO: an enterprise customer can configure SAML IdP metadata and perform a successful SSO login (IdP-initiated and SP-initiated tested).
SCIM provisioning: create/update/deactivate flows work end-to-end with group sync; deprovisioning removes console access within SLA (<= 5 minutes in test).
RBAC enforcement: authz-service enforces role checks on model invocation, console routes, and admin APIs; integration tests exist for each role.

Periodic access review: scheduled job produces an evidence bundle with user list, last-login timestamps, role assignments, group membership, and residency tag; bundle is signed and stored to audit bucket.
Reports: Compliance team can request report filtered by data residency and retention class; generated artifact contains cryptographic proof of generation time and signer id.
Operational: monitoring alerts fire if SCIM sync fails for >15 minutes or if SAML metadata fails to validate signatures.
Security review: completed and signed off before release to private customers (security_review_required=true).
technical_notes: Implementation outline: 1) RBAC: extend authz-service with a role graph and path-based permission checks. Store role assignments in user-store with residency tags. 2) SSO/SAML: reuse existing sso-proxy; add scheduled metadata fetcher and cert-rotation checklist; validate assertions with strict audience and recipient checks. 3) SCIM: adopt SCIM v2.0, implement idempotent PUT/POST handling, support group mappings in a declarative mapping file per-customer. Handle deprovisioning via 'active' flag + soft-delete window aligned to retention policies. 4) Access reviews: implement a report-generator service that queries user-store and logs, composes evidence bundle, signs bundle with KMS key, and writes to audit-bucket/<customer>/reviews/<yyyy-mm-dd>. Use event-driven triggers for ad-hoc reviews (webhook) and cron for scheduled quarterly reviews. 5) Tests: e2e with Okta and AzureAD, integration tests for sync latency and edge cases (email collisions, duplicate externalIds).
qa_steps: Configure a test IdP (Okta) with provided SP metadata and perform SP-initiated login.
Create a user in IdP, assign to a SCIM-provisioned group; verify user appears in Console and has group-derived roles.
Deactivate user in IdP; verify access revoked within deprovision SLA in test environment.
Run access-review job for test org and inspect signed evidence bundle in audit-bucket; validate signature using public key published in Confluence.
Simulate SCIM sync failure and confirm alert fires and ticket created in PagerDuty test channel.
